title: Wave-pinning crawler at low contractility repairs a cut front: the front splits into two competing polarity domains, one takes over, and the cell crawls on at 90-98% of its twin's speed. The linear twin never moves.
summary: World: the Camley et al. (2017) phase-field crawler with mass-conserved bistable polarity, per-body pools, rho*=0.2 and weak noise eta=2 (world.py). A mature half-moon crawling at 0.42 is cut at t=8 at the centre of its leading edge: a 30% sector (26-27% of the area, 31-32% of the protein, which leaves the cell), or a 15% sector on seed 2. The remaining polarity forms two lateral domains that pull the cell into a dumbbell. Within about 3 time units one domain takes over through the shared cytosolic pool and the cell crawls again as a single-front half-moon at 0.385-0.407, against its branched twin's 0.42. This holds on 3/3 seeds for the 30% cut, on 1/1 for the 15% cut, and without noise (eta=0, 0.40 vs 0.44) (cuts/*/cut.png; labkit packs pack_front vs pack_twin, seeds 0 and 1). At the paper's rho*=0.4 the same cuts end in a static, uniformly polarized disk or a fission into two such disks (parent finding). Limits: this is not re-nucleation of the front. Erasing the whole polarity domain (cuts/r2_s*_chem) kills the cell by t~9.4 on 2/2 seeds even with noise, because the low state is linearly stable. The cell's later reshaping is curvature flow plus protrusion, by construction. The repair is the winner-take-all competition of wave-pinned domains, a known property of mass-conserved polarity (Mori et al. 2008). The cell is planted (no S), and B is not claimed: the boundary is the Allen-Cahn contour. The matched linear-kinetics twin (KIN=1, the same rate, pack_linear) depolarizes and never moves, so neither M nor R exists without the bistable kinetics.

claims.statement: One planted crawler per run. It crawls as a single-front half-moon at 0.42 (>= 3.6 body lengths per run). After its leading edge is cut at t=8, the split polarity resolves into one front within ~3 time units and the same cell crawls on at 0.385-0.407 (twin 0.42). Seeds 0, 1 and 2 with a 30% sector, seed 2 with a 15% sector, and seed 0 without noise. Commands: labkit run of world.py with WORLD_P='{"cut_t":8.0,"cut_mode":"front"}' for pack_front and with no WORLD_P for pack_twin; cutrun.py world.py <seed> 8 18 <out> with WORLD_P='{"cut_mode":"front"}' for the side-by-side cut figures.
claims.track: seed 1, pack_front/seed1 track 0 (the only track, 91/91 frames): crawls left t=0-8, cut at t=8, two front domains t=8.6-10.2, one front again by t=11, crawls down t=11-18 (pack_front/seed1/sheet.png)

controls_run.R: pack_twin/seed0 and pack_twin/seed1: the undamaged twin, identical to pack_front until t=8; side-by-side twins in cuts/r2_s*_front30/cut.png. Polarity-erase arm cuts/r2_s0_chem and cuts/r2_s1_chem: fatal. rho*=0.4 contrast: parent 20261025T1915-c22-wavepin-front-cut-no-repair
controls_run.M: pack_linear/seed0 and pack_linear/seed1: linear-kinetics twin, no polarity, no motion

claims.bd_control: pack_linear (KIN=1: f = -125 (rho - m rho_cyt / 2), the linearization rate of the cubic, same diffusion and phase field): the cell depolarizes, stays round and moves 0.0 body lengths on 2/2 seeds, so neither M nor R can occur
